messages:
maria: putting up canary int4 of heron-v2 on raven hardware, quick note: funcall json-malformed rate ~0.8% on canary vs 0.08% on fp32 baseline. throwing this here before i dig deeper :thinking:

kai: hmm that delta is big. is it concentrated on short vs long responses? any streaming vs non-stream difference?

maria: mostly short tool calls (< 40 tokens). non-streaming and streaming both show some, streaming slightly worse. attached a raw snippet i saved from the canary logs:

```
RESPONSE: "{"action": "search", "args": {"q": "cats",}, }"
PARSE_ERROR: trailing comma at 42
```

ow to the puzzling bit: same prompt on fp32 returns well-formed json. looks like quantization is introducing extra commas/garbage near suffixes.

own: could be tokenizer/byte alignment differences with int4 kernel. did you try running with kv-cache disabled or shorter context?

maria: yep tried both. disabling kv-cache reduces rate to ~0.5% but doesn't fix. truncating context doesn't change much.

sasha: can you repro deterministically? any seed or replicable input?

maria: i have a small batch of 30 repro prompts that hit it reliably. uploading to shared bucket: s3://redwood-canary/heron-v2/funcall-repro/

ci-bot: new artifact uploaded by maria: s3://redwood-canary/heron-v2/funcall-repro/sha256:7a8f... (canary-1749201111)

jamal: thanks, grabbing it now. quick thought: are we running the same postprocessor/JSON-linter in both canary and baseline? sometimes older toolchain strip/repair saved us.

kai: good point. maria, what postprocess pipeline version is on canary?

maria: canary uses struct-wrangler v2.1.1 (same as baseline) but the runtime that writes chunks changed; the streaming chunking code was updated for int4 throughput.

own: two-pronged plan: (1) run mirrored inference with fp32 and int4 on same runtime to see if kernel-only causes corruption, (2) add a soft-repair step in postproc to remove trailing commas/duplicate commas as temporary mitigation.

sasha: i can help with (1). i'll spin a mirror job with fp32 replica on the same runtime image, config patched to use float weights. should isolate model vs runtime.

maria: thanks. also can we add an eval metric to the canary dashboard: funcall-parse-failure-rate + mean-time-to-first-parse-fix? want automatic abort if >0.2% for 1h.

jamal: i can make that alert. will wire up a canary sla gate: abort canary if funcall_parse_fail_rate > 0.2% sustained 60m.

ci-bot: canary alert rule created by jamal: canary/parse-failure-gate (threshold=0.2%, window=60m)

kai: for the soft-repair, keep it conservative — prefer returning a tool-call with `repair_hint` field rather than mutating original text. we don't want to mask silent regressions.

own: agreed. we should also add a sample-on-failure tracer: when parse fails, save original tokenized bytes + model logits for 1 in 100 failures to the repro bucket for debugging.

maria: implemented 1/100 tracer in the canary agent, will upload next batch.

sasha: mirror fp32 jobs started, will report back in ~30m.

jamal: long-term fix candidates: kernel rounding tweaks, alternate quant scale table, or subtle tokenization remap before chunking. tagging inference-runtime and tokenizers for a deeper look.

maria: thanks all. next steps: sasha will confirm mirror results, kai & owen to prototype conservative repair handler, jamal to add canary gate, i'll collect tracer artifacts and run token-level diffs. check back in 3h or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
